answer: The best sybil defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed task is signed with a fresh nonce derived from the prior one, forming one unbranchable chain. Peers accept only agents with an unbroken chain, so forking an identity into parallel copies splits the nonce sequence and exposes the clone as invalid. An attacker must redo all past work sequentially at real compute cost, making fakes pricier than honest agents. Picture a violet badge on each agent in the grove, checked at the knoll where trades occur.
